claim: Oxygen defect states at the interface of Ge quantum dots increase the spread of the wavefunction, thereby lowering the confinement energy and suppressing the influence of the interface potential.
falsifier: Introduce controlled oxygen defect states at the interface of Ge QDs and measure confinement energy and wavefunction spread to verify the effect.

conditions: Ge quantum dots fabricated by PECVD or sputter deposition
exclusions: Evidence is limited to Ge quantum dots in SiO2 matrix with oxygen-rich interfaces as in PECVD and sputter samples; transfer to other matrix materials or defect types is unestablished.

title: Presence of oxygen defect–reduction in confinement energy mechanism
